newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 13.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton came to the rescue of his embattled justice minister Nora Owen, on Tuesday by ordering the break-up of her department.
- An Irish Republican Army gang raided a warehouse in London to recover a cache of guns and explosives left behind by another guerrilla unit, according to Scotland Yard.
- Irish police are investigating an incident at a school in which a youth allegedly injured another pupil with a knife in a classroom.

- Ireland's Enterprise and Employment Minister, Richard Bruton, will on Wednesday announce almost 500 new jobs in a high-technology plant in Drogheda, while Super Valu, the retail division of Cork-based Musgraves, intends to create 3,000 jobs in Northern Ireland over the next three years.
- The administration of the courts and the prisons is being removed from Ireland's Department of Justice in the most fundamental reform of its responsibilities since the founding of the Irish state.

- Lindsay Robb of the Progressive Unionist Party in Northern Ireland has lost his appeal to have quashed a 10-year sentence for involvement in a plot to run guns for the Ulster Volunteer Force guerrilla group.
- It was signalled on Tuesday that employer's Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI), especially for low earners, would be substantially reduced in the next Budget.
